_howTo: Radio talks with Walla Walla. Each lesson has two: "start" is typed out on the slip as the lesson opens, and "check" frames the lesson's check: its first line is typed above the check's questions and its last line under the score. In the start talk, each turn has Walla Walla saying "them" and the player picking one of up to three "replies" (none means a plain "Roger. Over."); a reply can have a "back" line, and every reply leads on to the next turn.

turns.them: Harrow, Walla Walla. Tonight’s question sounds easy and isn’t: how high is that cloud? No balloon, no aeroplane. Just your eyes, four words of Latin, and, believe it or not, your hands.

replies.back: Four words of it, and friendly ones.

turns.them: The three floors of the sky, how the names are built, and three quick tricks. Questions at the end.
Harrow, Walla Walla. Quiz. Put every cloud on its floor.
Every floor called. Next lesson, the high clouds that tell tomorrow’s weather.
